paper_metadata.title: Early infarct FLAIR hyperintensity is associated with increased hemorrhagic transformation after thrombolysis

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used a consecutive recruitment strategy from two specialized stroke centers with clearly defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and well-described baseline characteristics. The sample is representative of the target population of acute stroke patients eligible for thrombolysis.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Consecutive stroke patients recruited between May 2008 and May 2010 from two stroke centers (Berlin... and Hamburg...)
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly identified as patients from two specific academic stroke centers.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Consecutive stroke patients... with known time of onset, who had magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before and 1 day after thrombolysis were included
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment is the gold standard for limiting selection bias in prognosis studies.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study design required both baseline and 24-hour follow-up MRI for inclusion. While this creates a 'completer' cohort, the short follow-up period (24 hours) in an inpatient setting typically results in very low attrition, and the reasons for exclusion (missing follow-up) are standard for this type of imaging study.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (FLAIR hyperintensity) was measured using a standardized qualitative method with two independent raters blinded to the outcome. Inter-rater reliability was high (kappa = 0.78).

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: FLAIR positivity, defined as a hyperintensity on acute FLAIR images corresponding (in shape and location) to the DWI lesion.
items.reasoning: The definition is clear and linked to the DWI lesion topography.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Two raters (blind to HT) independently identified FLAIR hyperintensity... Interrater agreement for FLAIR lesion hyperintensity was high (kappa = 0.78, P < 0.001).
items.reasoning: Blinding and high inter-rater reliability support the validity of the measurement.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Images were only rated FLAIR positive if both raters agreed on the presence of FLAIR hyperintensities
items.reasoning: The study uses a binary classification based on consensus, which is standard for this imaging marker.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Minimum MRI protocol included the following sequences: diffusion-weighted imaging, perfusion imaging, T2*, and FLAIR
items.reasoning: All patients underwent the same standardized MRI protocol.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: Of 109 patients... 30% were FLAIR positive (n = 33).
items.reasoning: PF data was available for all 109 patients included in the analysis.

items.label: Method used for missing data

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (HT) was defined using established radiological criteria (ECASS) and assessed on T2* MRI, which is a sensitive and objective method. Raters were blinded to the prognostic factor status.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: HT was assessed on T2* sequences based on CT definitions previously published [12]: hemorrhagic infarction (HI) was defined as either petechial without mass effect... or parenchymal hematoma (PH)
items.reasoning: The study uses the well-validated ECASS classification for HT.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Blinded to follow-up imaging, two raters (AK, MEbi) independently judged FLAIR positivity... HT was assessed on T2* sequences
items.reasoning: The use of T2* MRI (more sensitive than CT) and blinded assessment ensures high reliability.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Follow-up MRI examinations were performed typically within 24 h after the pre-treatment scan
items.reasoning: All patients were assessed using the same imaging modality at the same time point.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study adjusted for major confounders (NIHSS, DWI volume, glucose, reperfusion) in a multivariable model. However, the sample size (n=109) and the low number of outcome events (n=17) may limit the stability of the model (overfitting risk), and some variables like reperfusion were only available for a subset (n=90).

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: Along with FLAIR, we added known predictors of HT: NIHSS, DWI lesion volume, Wahlund score... serum glucose levels, and reperfusion
items.reasoning: The authors identified and measured the most clinically relevant confounders for HT.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: Wahlund score (a rating scale for age-related white matter changes)... Reperfusion was defined as a 75% reduction in perfusion deficit
items.reasoning: Confounders are defined using established scales or quantitative thresholds.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: perfusion deficit on MTT maps was defined as MTT > 6 s using Stroketool®
items.reasoning: Objective software-based measurements were used for imaging confounders.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Perfusion data were only available for Berlin patients (n = 90).
items.reasoning: One major confounder (reperfusion) was not measured for the entire cohort (missing for 19 patients).

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).

items.reasoning: Statistical adjustment was performed, although the event-to-variable ratio is low.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are appropriate for the study design. The authors report both univariate and multivariable results, including Odds Ratios and 95% Confidence Intervals. The high OR (18) and wide CI suggest a strong association but also reflect the small sample size.

items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Group comparison was made using Fisher's exact test and the Mann–Whitney U-test. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed...
items.reasoning: The analytical plan is clearly laid out.

items.reasoning: Variable selection was based on clinical knowledge of HT risk factors.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: Multivariable logistic regression analysis
items.reasoning: Logistic regression is appropriate for the binary outcome of HT.
